announced.basis: documents this watch saw appear between one run and the next. Everything present when the watch was seeded is deliberately absent here: it was already known and was never new.

as_of_means: The date of the last live crawl, not today. This feed goes visibly out of date rather than silently.

awaiting_minutes.basis: an agenda posted for a past date whose file id has no minutes alongside it in the town's listing. This is minutes against AGENDAS, not against meetings held -- the same proxy sources/data/minutes-coverage.csv rests on, and the town publishes nothing that reconciles the two.

first_seen_means: The day our crawler first saw a document. The town publishes no posting timestamp, so a gap between a meeting and its minutes appearing is an UPPER BOUND on how long the town took, never a measurement of it. Documents adopted when the watch was seeded have no first_seen and are excluded from every lag figure.
not_a_measurement: This file records what the Lunenburg Budget Project's crawler could see on the town's AgendaCenter on the date given. It is not a figure checked against a document, and it must not be presented beside one as the same kind of number.

recent.basis: one row per meeting from sources/data/meeting-register.csv -- the one record a meeting has -- for past meetings the town posted or published something about in the window; every artifact we hold for it is on the row. Newest activity first.

our_minutes.headline: Board put the track and field engineering article on the special town meeting warrant and rejected the park design article.
Committee voted to hire Rich Matthew as finance director and to request free cash for the special ed reserve fund.
School Committee unanimously approved a new director of finance and operations title and hired a temporary director.
Paraprofessional contract vote delayed again over salary-calculation errors; two placeholder warrant articles advanced
The school committee will hire its own next business administrator, deciding by vote next week after tonight's public interview.
A citizens' petition forced an earlier special town meeting to consider added state aid for the school budget.
The committee approved a spending plan and voted to send a warrant article to the Select Board for extra FY27 school funding.
Select Board moves toward a decision on demolishing or renovating the deteriorating TCP building
The board took the Flatill Road bridge land by eminent domain and tabled the DPW union contract over legal disputes.
Sewer Commission voted to send a delinquent Sunny Hill Road account to the tax collector with no payment plan.
Select Board recommended disapproval of the special ed reserve transfer and deferred budget and track articles for the Nov 17 special town meeting.
Finance Committee heard the stormwater utility, library, special education reserve and track articles; no article votes.
Parks Commission left field fees unchanged until the FY28 maintenance contract is known, and tabled Wallace Park lights.
Commission approved several septic and other compliance certificates and two NOIs, and continued most hearings to October 21.
Finance Committee recommended the new-state-aid school spending plan, but deferred the funding source for the rest of the warrant to town meeting itself.
Assessors heard a stormwater task force pitch a new utility fee shifting costs onto big paved lots
Trust Fund Commission voted unanimously to adopt nine governing documents, including the resident guide, operational manual and investment policy.
Committee declined to change float rules for non-LHS students; FY28 capital plan led by turf/track safety fix, no votes on priorities.
Conservation Commission approved several wetland filings, a revised Cowry ADA trail plan advanced, and $950 Hollis Road electrical work was approved.
Select Board put several articles on the Nov. 17 special town meeting warrant and held others pending information.
Select Board recommends a lower education-aid figure than the school committee for Thursday's special town meeting article.
Electronic voting machines can't be discontinued for the August special election — the state says they're mandatory.
The Select Board reconstituted the Personnel Committee as a five-member body and filled its seats along with most other town board vacancies.
Board set an August 8 special election for two vacant seats and completed the town manager's annual review
Select Board ratified a new multi-year police union contract and raised trash bag fees
Select Board advised the building committee to fold PACK studio space into phases one and two, and kept comparable-communities list with Gardner added back.

meetings.body_as_printed: NDA Lunenburg Public Library Board of Trustees Strategic Plan Subcommittee

our_minutes.headline: Trust Fund Commission voted to advertise its funds, file its vacancy bylaw text, and move meetings to Wednesdays.
Stormwater task force reworked its slide deck to present neutral funding choices for the town's MS4 compliance to Select Board and FinCom.
PACC voted by roll call, 3 yes, to ask Town Meeting to fully fund its FY27 PEG access budget from retained earnings.
PACC will seek a November special town meeting warrant for more money as FY27 salaries run tight
PACC backed a salary-line warrant request for the November warrant; its longtime chair announced resignation.
Planning Board approved the 30 School Street food pantry site plan with conditions and backed housekeeping zoning changes.
Personnel Committee dropped the two-of-three voting change and began shaping a warrant article on job-description review and a class and comp study.
Sewer Commission discussed raising the late-payment interest rate and demand fee to match nearby towns; no vote was taken.
Commission votes to seek a joint meeting with the School Committee over trust funds held under the town's EIN
Trust Fund chair disputes school committee's control over scholarship funds, citing state trust law
ZBA voted to grant a variance letting a modular food pantry building be placed at 30 School Street.
Sewer Commission approved moving money into the connection fees line to pay Leominster's per-connection charges.
Assessors tabled a plan to expand veterans' property-tax exemptions until the chair weighs in
Board withholds releasing a tax lien on a Chapter Land property until the owner pays years of back taxes owed.

upcoming.basis: an agenda posted for a date on or after as_of. An agenda is not a guarantee the meeting happens, and a meeting can be held with no agenda posted.
